title: fmt.Sprintf misses tainted Stringer struct fields
claim: A direct fmt.Sprintf call that formats a tainted Stringer struct field produces SQL with no taint because only top-level string and byte-slice arguments are inspected.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -timeout 8m -count=1 -run '^TestParity' -v ./iast/propagation

title: fmt.Sprintf taints an argument that emitted no bytes
claim: A zero-precision string directive emits no user bytes but the resulting clean SQL query is marked tainted and collected as unsafe SQL evidence.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -timeout 8m -count=1 -run '^TestParity' -v ./iast/propagation

title: strings.Map retains taint after deleting all tainted runes
claim: Deleting every tainted rune with strings.Map yields constant SQL text that remains fully tainted and is collected as unsafe SQL evidence.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -timeout 8m -count=1 -run '^TestParity' -v ./iast/propagation
